Escalated: exact unresolved proof obligation: If the knot has exactly two boundary slopes, non-thinness forces at least two distinct strict edge slopes of the enhanced Newton polygon. Since every knot also has boundary slope zero, the two slopes must include zero; the source's ideal-point argument makes zero strict. A connected incompressible surface realizing zero is either separating or nonseparating. In the latter case the longitudinal-surface lemma makes it isotopic to the fiber, contradicting strictness, so the separating alternative follows. If the knot has more than two slopes, the second alternative holds. The enhanced thin theorem, Culler–Shalen surface theorem, and Nielsen/Waldhausen input remain escalated, so this result is escalated.
